name: The Hollowed

relationships.label: Vel-Thara the Unmade creates the Hollowed — she claims every soul that completes the erosion, leaving an empty vessel animated by residual moon energy.
The Hollowed are the end state of the Pale-Touched transformation — Stage Six, when the person is consumed entirely and only the light remains.
The Oathbound Remnants mercy-kill the Hollowed as a sacred duty — naming each one before releasing it, because no Greyvasti should remain unremembered.
The Sunken Quarter of Greyvast hosts the densest concentration of Hollowed in Northern Velkaris — its drowned ruins are a drift-field of empty bodies.
Most Hollowed are former Greyvasti who return to their drowned city without knowing why, wandering the Sunken Quarter's submerged streets driven by residual memory.

description: The Hollowed are what remains when a human is completely consumed by soul erosion — empty bodies animated by residual moon energy, drifting through ruins without purpose or awareness. They do not attack. They do not flee. They walk toward moon fragments, silently, endlessly. Proximity to a Hollowed accelerates soul erosion in living beings, making them dangerous not for what they do but for what they are. The Oathbound Remnants mercy-kill them as a sacred duty, naming each one before releasing it.
excerpt: Empty bodies animated by residual moon energy — former humans who drift toward moon fragments in silence. The Remnants name each one before releasing it.
content:
The first thing you notice about a Hollowed is the silence. No footsteps, no breathing, no rustle of clothing against skin — because there is no friction, no effort, no will behind the motion. They simply drift. Their feet find the ground without impact. The mist parts around them without resistance. They move like a thought unfinished.

They walk toward light. Not sunlight — they are indifferent to the sun. Moon fragment light. A Hollowed in the Sunken Quarter will turn its face toward the drowned crater of Greyvast's central square, where the largest fragment lies submerged. It will walk into the water and keep walking until its head disappears beneath the surface. The body does not drown. It does not resurface. It simply continues, deeper, drawn by a pull that no longer requires lungs to obey.

Proximity corruption is the true danger. A living human within twenty feet of a Hollowed will feel it — a humming in the bones, a thinning at the temples, the same Stage One symptoms that mark the beginning of the Pale-Touched transformation. The longer you stay, the faster the erosion. A Hollowed is not a predator. It is a leak. A wound in the world that spreads Yssara's touch to anyone who comes too close.

The Oathbound Remnants have developed a ritual for dealing with them. When a Remnant finds a Hollowed, she names it. She does not know the name — she guesses, based on the shape of the face, the remnants of a scar, the way the fingers are curled. She says the name aloud. She says: I remember you. And then she drives her blade through the skull, where the light is brightest. The Hollowed does not react. The light does not fade immediately. But the Remnant has done her duty — the name was spoken, and Mourne will not take it.

No one knows how many Hollowed walk the ruins of Northern Velkaris. The Sunken Quarter alone is estimated to hold hundreds. They drift past each other without acknowledgment, bodies that were once neighbors, friends, family — now strangers to everything except the light they follow.

name: The Fracture Wyrm

relationships.label: The Fracture Wyrms emerged during the Celestial Fracture, driven from deep underground by the seismic shockwaves and the strange energy radiating from the fallen moon fragments.
The Tide-Weavers actively hunt Fracture Wyrms — the creatures collapse excavation tunnels, destroy salvage equipment, and consume valuable moon fragments before they can be recovered.
The Pale Dominion venerates Fracture Wyrms as Yssara's sacred guardians, believing the creatures were sent to protect the moon fragments from desecration.
The Sunken Quarter of Greyvast hosts several Fracture Wyrm nests — the submerged ruins provide shelter and a steady supply of moon fragments washed down from the crater.
Fracture Wyrms are drawn to Yssara's power, instinctively seeking out moon fragments to consume — the larger the fragment, the stronger the pull, and the larger the wyrm grows.

description: The Fracture Wyrm is a massive serpentine creature that burrowed up from the deep earth when the moon fragments struck. It consumes moon fragments and grows larger — the oldest specimens exceed 200 feet. The Tide-Weavers hunt them as pests that collapse excavations. The Pale Dominion venerates them as sacred guardians of Yssara's fragments. The wyrms are neither — they are ancient, hungry animals responding to a geological disruption they do not understand.
excerpt: Massive serpentine creatures that burrowed up during the Celestial Fracture, consuming moon fragments and growing to enormous size. Hunted by the Tide-Weavers. Venerated by the Pale Dominion. Neither is correct.
content:
The ground hums before it breaks. That is the only warning. A low vibration that rises through the boots, through the knees, through the spine — and then the stone splits, and the wyrm rises.

Fracture Wyrms do not burst from the ground like monsters in a children's tale. They emerge slowly, deliberately, their pale-grey scales grinding against the rock with a sound like wet gravel. First the head — broad, flat, eyeless, a blunt wedge of bone and muscle. Then the body, segment after segment, each ringed with crystalline growths that glow faintly in the dark. The wyrm does not look at the humans frozen before it. It does not see them. It senses only one thing: the moon fragment.

The worm ignores everything else. It will slide past a row of armed Tide-Weavers to reach a fragment the size of a fist. It will crush a supply cart without noticing. It will coil around a building to get closer to the light. When it reaches the fragment, it opens its mouth — a vertical split in the underside of the head — and draws the fragment inside with a suction that pulls dust and pebbles from the floor. The crystalline growths along its body flare briefly. The worm grows a fraction of an inch. Then it turns, slowly, and descends back into the dark.

The Pale Dominion insists that these creatures are sacred. They argue that the wyrm's attraction to moon fragments proves Yssara's design — the wyrms collect what is holy and carry it deep into the earth where it cannot be desecrated. The Tide-Weavers, who lose equipment and crew to collapsing tunnels every season, disagree. They have harpoons. They have explosives. They have a very practical understanding of what happens when you confuse hunger with divinity.

A fully grown Fracture Wyrm has never been killed. The Tide-Weavers have killed juveniles — specimens under fifty feet — by collapsing tunnels on them and waiting for the crushing weight to do its work. The adults are too large to trap, too deep to follow, and too indifferent to fight. They do not defend themselves. They do not attack. They simply eat, and grow, and descend, and the only evidence they existed at all is the hole they leave behind.

name: The Grief-Echo

relationships.label: The Grief-Echoes were born from the Celestial Fracture — the psychic shock of the moon shattering imprinted the death-memories of thousands onto the landscape itself.
The Greyvasti consider Grief-Echoes sacred — these are the unremembered dead, souls whose names were never carved, playing out their final moments for anyone who will witness.
Grief-Echoes are a manifestation of Vel-Thara's domain — she is the goddess of what is lost and unmade, and these psychic remnants are her silent chorus.
Grief-Echoes cluster on the outskirts of Ashenveil, drawn to the concentration of Greyvasti refugees — the city's edge is a wall of repeating death-screams at night.

description: Grief-Echoes are psychic remnants of people who died during the Celestial Fracture — not physical bodies but pure emotional memory given form. They replay their death-moment on an endless loop, and anyone nearby experiences the memory involuntarily. Prolonged exposure causes memory fragmentation in the living. The Greyvasti consider them sacred: these are the unremembered dead, souls whose names were never carved.
excerpt: Psychic remnants of Fracture victims — pure grief given form, replaying death-memories on loop. The Greyvasti consider them sacred.
content:
You do not see a Grief-Echo. You experience it.

The first sign is always a sound. A footstep on gravel that should not be there. A breath where no one is standing. A voice calling a name you do not recognize — but the name settles in your chest like a stone you have been carrying your whole life. And then the memory takes you.

You are standing in a street that collapsed. The buildings are falling sideways, slowly, the way they do when time stretches before impact. The sky is splitting. Someone is running beside you — a woman whose face you have never seen but whose terror you know as intimately as your own heartbeat. She falls. You feel her hand slip from yours. You feel the rubble close over her. And then the loop resets, and you are standing in the same street, and the buildings are falling sideways again.

A Grief-Echo does not speak. It does not move. It is a fixed point in space where a death occurred — a tear in reality through which the same moment pours forever. The Greyvasti mark these locations with small cairns. They do not disturb them. They do not try to banish them. The Grief-Echo is a witness that cannot stop witnessing itself, and the Greyvasti believe that to silence it would be to kill the person a second time.

The danger is proximity. A living human who stands within a Grief-Echo's radius for more than a few minutes will begin to absorb fragments of the memory as their own. They will flinch at sounds that do not exist. They will forget where they are. They will call out names that belong to strangers. The Ashenveil border patrol rotates its sentries every two hours to prevent permanent memory damage. The cairns multiply each season. The dead keep dying, and the echoes keep playing, and there is nothing to do but listen.

name: The Shard-Stalker

relationships.label: Shard-Stalkers hunt the Pale-Touched exclusively, drawn by the silver glow of their veins — they ignore all other prey with unnerving single-mindedness.
The Pale Dominion considers Shard-Stalkers demonic — the creatures hunt their living saints, and the Dominion interprets this as a direct attack by Vel-Thara on Yssara's chosen.
The Oathbound Remnants follow Shard-Stalkers to locate Pale-Touched who have wandered into dangerous territory — the hunters always know where the prey is.
Shard-Stalkers are endemic to Northern Velkaris, having evolved specifically in the post-Fracture ecosystem to exploit the unique niche of moon-tainted prey.

description: The Shard-Stalker is a predatory creature that evolved in the post-Fracture ecosystem of Northern Velkaris to hunt the Pale-Touched. Fast, spider-like, and completely silent, it is drawn exclusively to the silver glow of moon-tainted veins and ignores all other living beings. The Pale Dominion considers it demonic — a creature sent by Vel-Thara to harvest Yssara's saints. The Oathbound Remnants, characteristically pragmatic, follow Shard-Stalkers to locate Pale-Touched who need mercy-killing.
excerpt: A predator evolved to hunt the Pale-Touched — silent, spider-like, drawn to silver-glowing veins. The Remnants follow them to find their prey.
content:
The Shard-Stalker does not hunt like an animal. It hunts like an instrument. It moves with a precision that suggests purpose rather than hunger — each leg placed with mechanical exactness, each pause calculated, each shift in direction a response to something invisible to human eyes.

It is the silver glow. The Stalker sees what humans cannot — the vein-light of the Pale-Touched, visible through walls, through mist, through stone. A Pale-Touched in Stage Three or beyond radiates a signature that the Stalker can track from over a mile away. The creature does not need to see its prey. It follows the light the way a moth follows the moon, except this moth is eight-legged and silent and its arrival means death.

The stalker's body is angular, chitinous, segments of pale grey that blend perfectly into frost-covered ruins. It has too many joints in its legs — the angles are wrong, the movement uncanny. It does not click or scrape when it walks. The silence is deliberate, biological, a hunting adaptation so refined that a full-grown Shard-Stalker can cross a room of loose gravel without shifting a single stone.

When it finds its prey, it does not attack immediately. It watches. It waits. The Shard-Stalker has no interest in a fight — it wants certainty. It follows the Pale-Touched for hours, sometimes days, learning their patterns, until it knows the exact moment when the prey will be alone, still, unaware. And then it moves, faster than the eye can track, and the Pale-Touched's silver glow extinguishes forever.

The Pale Dominion has declared the Shard-Stalker a demon, a direct agent of Vel-Thara sent to harvest Yssara's living saints. Dominion hunter-parties track and kill Stalkers whenever they are found. The Oathbound Remnants, who hold no such theology, have developed a different relationship with the creatures. They follow them. A Shard-Stalker always knows where the Pale-Touched are, and a Remnant who trails a Stalker at a safe distance will eventually find someone who needs naming. The arrangement is not cooperation — the Stalker does not know it is being followed — but it is useful. The Remnants call the Stalker the Remnant's Compass, and they pray it never learns to hunt them instead.
